description: Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes — also known as "El Mencho" — was the leader of the notorious Jalisco New Generation Cartel prior to his death on Sunday.

description: The U.S. men's hockey team beat Canada on Sunday to win its first Olympic gold medal since the "Miracle on Ice" in 1980. Kelly O'Grady reports.

description: Russia fired scores of missiles and drones at targets across Ukraine Sunday. Holly Williams is in Kyiv with more.

description: The United States stands at the brink of a major conflict in the Middle East with the Iranian regime grappling with domestic discontent and the threat of U.S. strikes. Charlie D'Agata reports.

description: Mexican security forces killed Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes, also known as "El Mencho," during an operation in the western state of Jalisco, Mexico's Ministry of Defense said Sunday. Violent clashes erupted in parts of western Mexico amid the operation. Americans caught in the chaos have been told to shelter in place. Willie James Inman reports.
title: Violence in Mexico after cartel leader "El Mencho" killed in military operation

description: A massive winter storm has begun to impact the East Coast, with heavy snow, brutal wind and dangerous flooding expected for several states. Shanelle Kaul, Andrew Kozak and Jason Allen have the latest.

description: A defense lawyers group has posted a tracking tool to enable users to check on the status of some of the controversial prosecutions attempted by DOJ in the first year of Trump's second term.

description: More than 8,000 flights have already been canceled through Monday due to the winter storm impacting the Northeast. More delays and cancellations are expected. description: More than 50 million people in the Northeast are under blizzard warnings as a dangerous, rapidly strengthening winter storm moves up the coast. Emergency declarations have been made in several states. Shanelle Kaul reports on the deteriorating conditions and Andrew Kozak has a look at the forecast.
title: 50 million under blizzard warnings, NYC issues travel ban as nor'easter arrives

title: Book excerpt: "We the Women" by Norah O'Donnell

description: The CBS News journalist's new book tells the often-overlooked stories of women who helped shape our nation, from the single female whose name appears on the Declaration of Independence, to the first Black woman to argue a case before the Supreme Court.
title: Norah O'Donnell on "We the Women," about the unsung heroines of America

description: In her new book, "We the Women," CBS News' Norah O'Donnell tells the overlooked stories of women who have helped shape our nation, from the single female whose name appears on the Declaration of Independence, to the first Black woman to argue a case before the Supreme Court. O'Donnell talks with correspondent Mo Rocca about being shocked by how much she didn't know of these women's contributions; the role of women in journalism today; and why she is optimistic about the future.
title: Norah O'Donnell on "We the Women," about the unsung heroines of America

description: For the past 33 years, mailman Joe DiTore has truly delivered for the residents of Demarest, New Jersey, as a helpful hand and watchful eye to everyone on his route. And now that he is retiring, the people on DiTore's route shared with Steve Hartman some of the many ways he was a source of comfort and inspiration.
title: How one mailman handled with extreme care

description: The Australian-born actress earned an Academy Award nomination for her powerful performance as a mother stretched to the limits.
title: Rose Byrne on playing a woman at the end of her rope in "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You"

description: In this web exclusive, Rose Byrne, an Oscar nominee for best actress for her performance in Mary Bronstein's "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You," talks with Tracy Smith about her response to the character of Linda, a woman at the end of her rope. She also talks about her early years in Hollywood, including her friendship with fellow Australian Heath Ledger, and her experience playing comedy with "Bridesmaids."
title: Extended interview: Rose Byrne

description: Australian-born actress Rose Byrne earned an Academy Award nomination for her powerful performance in the drama "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You," playing a mother stretched to the limits. She talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about playing a woman losing all sense of control. Byrne also discusses her early years in Hollywood and the help she received from fellow Aussie Heath Ledger; and how she branched off from working in dramas like the TV series "Damages," to comedies like "Bridesmaids."
title: Rose Byrne on playing a woman at the end of her rope in "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You"

description: A man was shot and killed at Mar-a-Lago early on Sunday after unlawful entry on the property, authorities said. The FBI, Secret Service and Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office held a news conference to provide updates. President Trump was not in Florida this weekend.
title: Authorities provide update after man is shot and killed at Mar-a-Lago

description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former Prince Andrew, was arrested in England Thursday on suspicion of misconduct in public office stemming from his involvement with the late financier Jeffrey Epstein. Mountbatten-Windsor has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing. Elizabeth Palmer reports on reaction to the arrest, which has raised questions about Epstein scandal-related justice in the United States.
title: Fallout from the arrest of Andrew stemming from Jeffrey Epstein

description: For six decades, the investigative journalist – subject of the documentary "Cover-Up" – has exposed corruption, war crimes, and political scandals. He talks about his career; why, at age 88, he's still loves being a reporter; and where he believes America stands now.
title: Seymour Hersh: A reporter's reporter

description: For six decades, Seymour Hersh's reporting for such publications as The New York Times and The New Yorker has changed public opinion and government policy – from documenting the My Lai massacre during the Vietnam War, to uncovering torture by American service members at the Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq. "60 Minutes" correspondent Lesley Stahl talks with the Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist about his career exposing corruption, and where he believes America stands now. She also talks with Laura Poitras, co-director of a new documentary on Hersh, "Cover-Up," about putting the reporter with a reputation for crankiness on camera.
title: Seymour Hersh, a reporter's reporter

description: "Sunday Morning" remembers some of the notable figures who left us this week, including Academy Award-winning actor Robert Duvall.
title: Passage: In memoriam

description: "Sunday Morning" looks back on the life of the Baptist minister, civil rights leader and social justice activist, whose trailblazing presidential campaigns, built on a message of economic support and faith-based compassion, fostered his so-called "Rainbow Coalition."
title: Remembering The Rev. Jesse Jackson, an American original

description: Mark Whitaker looks back on the life of The Rev. Jesse Jackson, the Baptist minister, civil rights leader and social justice activist, whose trailblazing presidential campaigns, built on a message of economic support and faith-based compassion, fostered his so-called "Rainbow Coalition."
title: Remembering The Rev. Jesse Jackson

description: As the Milano Cortina Winter Games draw to a close, skiers Mikaela Shiffrin and Breezy Johnson, figure skater Ilia Malinin, and bobsledder Elana Meyers Taylor talk about the Olympic-level pressure they endured in their quest for gold, while grappling with a vast range of emotions on the world's biggest sports stage. Seth Doane reports.
title: Athletes describe emotional journeys as 2026 Winter Olympics draw to a close

description: A man in his early 20s was shot and killed early Sunday morning after an "unauthorized entry" into the secure perimeter at President Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate, the U.S. Secret Service said.
title: Man shot, killed at Mar-a-Lago perimeter, Secret Service says

description: In 1968, a group of artists, activists, and community members founded the Studio Museum in Harlem. It was a space not just for displaying works celebrating the contributions of African-American artists, but also to foster up-and-coming artists through a residency program. Now, following a seven-year, $160 million renovation, the Studio Museum has reopened. Nancy Giles pays a visit.
title: The legacy of the Studio Museum in Harlem

description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.
title: Almanac: February 22

description: After decades of American children routinely receiving polio vaccines, the virus that had doomed many to paralysis was nearly eliminated in the United States. But vaccine avoidance today may allow the crippling disease to return.
title: How safe is America from polio?

description: In this web exclusive, famed violinist Itzhak Perlman talks with CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jonathan LaPook about his experience after contracting polio as a child, several years before the development of a polio vaccine, and the obstacles in life to which he has had to adjust because of his disability. He has advice for those who question taking the vaccine. He also talks about the effect of music on the brain, and how he wishes to be remembered.
title: Extended interview: Itzhak Perlman

description: After decades of American children routinely receiving polio vaccines, the virus that had doomed many to paralysis was nearly eliminated in the United States. But vaccine avoidance today may allow the crippling disease to return. CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jonathan LaPook talks with David Oshinsky, author of "Polio: An American Story," and with violin virtuoso Itzhak Perlman, who contracted polio as a child, about how parents opting out of vaccinations for their children could affect polio rates here.
title: How safe is America from polio?

description: The 22-year-old Gu, American-born but competing for her mother's homeland of China, is already the most decorated freeskier in the short history of the sport at the Olympics.
title: U.S.-born skier Eileen Gu defends Olympic ski halfpipe gold at Winter Games

description: A teenage girl goes missing. Will evidence on a secluded beach reveal what happened? "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green reports.

description: A soldier goes on the run after his wife is murdered. With him, his 17-year-old girlfriend. What does she know? "48 Hours" correspondent Peter Van Sant reports.

description: In April 2024, college student Sade Robinson, 19, went on a first date and never came home. Her car was found set on fire 3 miles from her apartment. Using data from an app on her phone, law enforcement began to piece together where she went — and who she was with.
title: Cell phone app, security video critical in helping solve teen's murder

description: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said in a statement that TSA and Customs and Border Protection "are prioritizing the general traveling population at our airports and ports of entry and suspending courtesy and special privilege escorts."
title: DHS suspending TSA PreCheck, Global Entry programs amid partial shutdown
